understanding: The master maintains an in-memory registration table, leader-selection flags, RPC clients, and ping-derived availability metadata. Registration, initial leadership RPCs, monitoring, and replacement selection can update this metadata. GetLeader exposes the first marked leader without waiting for initialization; GetReplicaList waits for the initial ping pass. These observations establish master-local metadata semantics, not completed replica authority transitions or current reachability.

activities.purpose: Select and expose master-local leader metadata and request replica leadership.
activities.realization_summary: Registration can mark an initial candidate. Bootstrap and replacement selection call Replica.BeTheLeader and interpret its reply. Monitoring clears marked leaders on ping errors. GetLeader returns the first marked index.
variants: Configured initial leader versus minimum measured latency.
BeTheLeader reply names the contacted replica implicitly or another replica explicitly.
Replacement tries nextLeader before scanning registered RPC clients.
unknowns: Replica.BeTheLeader and reply helper semantics are unread; RPC success does not establish completed protocol authority.
The selected deployment's configured leader and returned leadership variants are unknown.

activities.purpose: Maintain the master registration directory and expose participant readiness and availability metadata.
activities.realization_summary: The constructor fixes N and allocates participant arrays. Register assigns indices by address-port identity; GetReplicaList publishes the directory and availability flags after initial monitoring. This is directory management; protocol configuration activation is not established.
variants: Repeated address-port registration reuses an existing index.
Readiness depends on registered count equaling N.
unknowns: How replicas consume this directory as protocol membership remains unread.
No removal or resizing mechanism appears in this file; repository-wide participant-change applicability remains unresolved.

behaviors.protocol_context: One master process with constructor-supplied N and leader configuration.
behaviors.trigger: Registration request containing Addr and Port.
implementation_guards: Reuses an index for an exact formatted address-port match.
Returns Ready=true only when registered count equals N.
writes: nodeList, addrList, portList for new registrations
external_effects: Runs an operating-system ping command for a new address.
Calls master.Fatal if the ping command fails.
Returns directory, replica index, and local initial-leader indication when ready.
important_branches: New identities extend preallocated slices; no explicit capacity guard precedes extension.
Empty Addr is replaced with localhost only for the latency probe.
Successful probe output is split and indexed; ParseFloat errors are ignored.
Configured selection marks only a matching registering caller.
Latency selection marks the caller only if its index is the computed minimum.
Existing registrations may repeat candidate marking after the directory is ready.
async_boundaries: The external ping command runs while master.lock is held.
RPC handlers may overlap with bootstrap and monitoring.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Can mark an initial leader candidate before a leadership RPC completes.

existing_protections: Address-port deduplication preserves an existing registration index.
Mutex serializes registration against handlers that use the same lock.
unknowns: Caller constraints preventing more than N distinct registrations are unread.
Latency command output assumptions and Fatal behavior are not established by this file.
Registration reply consumers and their interpretation of IsLeader are unread.

behaviors.execution_owner: Master startup and its spawned run goroutine
behaviors.protocol_context: Fresh master state with finishInit=false, nextLeader=-1, and N-sized RPC and status arrays.
implementation_guards: Polls registered count under master.lock until it equals N.
Retries each failed replica RPC dial before advancing.
Invokes initial BeTheLeader only for a marked index.
Sets finishInit only after the initial ping pass returns.
writes: leader flags when the leadership reply redirects
external_effects: Registers master RPC handlers and serves HTTP.
Dials replica RPC endpoints at registered port plus 1000.
Broadcasts initCond after initial availability computation.
important_branches: Failed dials retry indefinitely with sleeps.
Initial BeTheLeader error invokes master.Fatal.
A reply naming another leader clears the contacted index and marks the returned index.
A redirect to a lower index rewinds the dialing loop.
RPC registration and HTTP serving return errors are not handled in this file.
async_boundaries: Run spawns the bootstrap and monitoring goroutine while serving RPC requests.
Sleep, dial, and leadership RPC calls can delay initialization.
Initial ping calls execute while master.lock is held.

cross_activity_effects.A4: Releases GetReplicaList waiters after initial ping metadata has been computed.

existing_protections: Condition-variable publication occurs under the associated mutex.
Initial redirect clears the previously contacted leader mark.
unknowns: Leadership reply construction, normalization, and returned-index constraints are unread.
Bootstrap leader updates occur outside master.lock; concurrent registration and query effects require separate analysis.
RPC timeouts and server-side leadership completion semantics are unknown.

behaviors.execution_owner: Master.run goroutine through its pingNode closure
behaviors.protocol_context: Initial ping pass and later sequential monitoring passes over nodes.
behaviors.trigger: Ping invocation for replica index i.
implementation_guards: Only a ping error at an index currently marked leader sets new_leader.
writes: new_leader on error at a marked leader
important_branches: Successful call stores alive[i]=true.
Error stores alive[i]=false.
Error at a marked leader additionally clears its mark and requests replacement selection for that pass.
async_boundaries: Each synchronous ping RPC may delay subsequent replicas.
The initial pass holds master.lock; periodic passes do not.

cross_activity_effects.A4: Updates the availability flags copied by GetReplicaList.

existing_protections: An observed ping failure clears that index's existing leader mark.
unknowns: Replica.Ping implementation and meaning of successful completion are unread.
No observation timestamps or generations are stored.
Periodic writes are not protected by the mutex used by query handlers.

behaviors.execution_owner: Master.run monitoring loop and its beTheLeader closure
behaviors.trigger: A periodic ping pass sets new_leader after a marked leader's ping fails.
implementation_guards: Resets new_leader before each periodic pass.
Skips replacement if the pass did not set new_leader.
Contacts a candidate only when its alive flag is true.
important_branches: Tries nextLeader first when it is not -1.
Falls back to scanning nodes after preferred-candidate failure.
Stops on the first successful leadership RPC.
A returned Leader other than -1 determines the marked index.
Replacement success does not explicitly clear other leader flags.
If all attempts fail, the next pass resets the trigger; absence of any mark alone does not trigger another attempt.
async_boundaries: Sleeps three seconds before each monitoring pass.
existing_protections: Candidates with a false availability flag are skipped.
A failed leadership RPC does not mark the contacted candidate through this closure.
unknowns: Whether another mechanism retries replacement after every candidate fails is unknown.
Reply redirection is not visibly checked against availability or array bounds.
Master-local marking does not establish completion of a replica authority transition.

implementation_guards: Holds master.lock while scanning leader flags.
Stops at the first true flag.
writes: reply.LeaderId when a true flag is found
external_effects: Returns nil error, including when no leader flag is true.
important_branches: A true flag causes the reply to name its index.
No true flag leaves the supplied reply unchanged.
No finishInit or alive check is performed.
async_boundaries: May overlap with bootstrap and periodic metadata writers that do not hold master.lock.
existing_protections: Uses the same mutex as registration.
unknowns: RPC reply defaults and caller handling of an unchanged reply are unread.
The client-visible guarantee attributed to LeaderId is unknown.

behaviors.protocol_context: Master registration directory and sampled availability metadata.
implementation_guards: Acquires master.lock and waits in a loop until finishInit is true.
Sets Ready according to registered count equaling N.
external_effects: Returns newly allocated address and availability slices with corresponding indices.
important_branches: Waits until bootstrap publishes initial ping completion.
Copies stored availability values without issuing fresh pings.
async_boundaries: Condition-variable wait releases and reacquires master.lock.
Periodic monitoring can update alive without the handler's mutex.
existing_protections: Looped condition wait handles wakeups before initialization is complete.
Fresh reply slices avoid directly returning the stored availability slice.
unknowns: The response is not established as a coherent snapshot of one periodic ping pass.
Consumers' treatment of Ready and AliveList is unread.

facts.meaning: The master has assigned a formatted address-port identity an index in its registration directory.
facts.validity_context: After the registration handler has populated the directory entry. This does not establish successful replica startup, protocol membership activation, or current availability.
facts.durability: In-memory only in the supplied source.
facts.recovery: No restoration path is shown; a fresh constructor creates an empty directory.
unknowns: Caller registration retries and restart identity semantics are unread.

facts.meaning: The master currently marks a replica index as a selected leader in its local metadata.
facts.validity_context: While the corresponding leader flag remains true. Registration can establish this mark before any leadership RPC. The mark alone establishes neither unique leadership nor completed replica authority.
facts.recovery: Fresh startup initializes flags to false and can mark candidates through registration and leadership replies.
unknowns: Consumers outside GetLeader and the master loop are unread.
Concurrent visibility is unresolved because not all writers hold master.lock.

facts.meaning: For a replica index, the master has stored whether the most recently processed Ping call returned without error.
facts.validity_context: After a ping result has been assigned to alive[index], until another result replaces it. It describes a completed call outcome, not continued reachability or legal protocol participation.
facts.durability: In-memory only; no timestamp or generation accompanies the boolean.
facts.recovery: Bootstrap recomputes values through an initial ping pass.
unknowns: The false constructor value does not distinguish an unobserved replica from a failed ping.
Remote Ping behavior and periodic-read synchronization are unresolved.

facts.meaning: The bootstrap goroutine completed its initial pass of ping calls over nodes and published initialization completion.
facts.validity_context: After finishInit is set under master.lock. Completion includes ping errors and does not assert that all replicas are alive or that leadership replacement has completed.
facts.durability: In-memory monotonic flag within the shown process lifetime.
facts.recovery: A fresh master starts with finishInit=false and repeats bootstrap.
unknowns: No bounded initialization duration is established; dialing and RPC calls can delay publication.

surfaces.reason: The supplied full master implementation supports mapping local metadata producers, bootstrap publication, monitoring, replacement selection, and both query consumers. Remote RPC completion semantics, helper behavior, and downstream interpretation remain explicit unknowns.

delta.rationale: Expand only the focused master surface and its directly connected registration producer. Preserve distinctions between local leader marking, leadership RPC completion, ping outcomes, and initialization publication. Record the synchronization and initial-versus-replacement branch differences descriptively without deriving obligations or claiming defects.

limitations: Only master/master.go was supplied as semantic evidence; replica RPC handlers, reply helpers, deployment callers, and query consumers remain unread.
No normative contract establishes that master-local leader metadata implies exclusive or completed protocol authority.
Mapping this surface records implementation understanding, not verified correctness, race reproduction, or complete protocol coverage.
